candidates.text: Jacolby Satterwhite - A Metta Prayer New York-based artist Jacolby Satterwhite’s A Metta Prayer (2023) is a multimedia, site-specific installation that was projected onto the walls of the Great Hall at the Metropolitan Museum of Art (The Met) in Manhattan. In an excerpt from the 21-minute, six-channel video, enter a virtual universe that brings together music, choreography, and animation in ecstatic scenes that celebrate hope, joy, and liberation. Satterwhite’s time-based piece echoes the grammar of endless-runner video games but eschews the gratuitous violence and exploitation that is common to this genre. Channeling the Buddhist Metta prayer of loving-kindness, the artist creates a mantra of his own, inspired by queer freedom of existence and expression. A Metta Prayer features Satterwhite collaborators including musicians Solange Knowles, Kelsey Lu and Moses Sumney, as well as drag artist Laveau Contraire, queer wrestling collective Choke Hole, and dance artist O'Shae Sibley. Over the last few years, Satterwhite has been fighting a public battle with complications due to cancer, and he is the inaugural recipient of the newly established Artists Living with Cancer Grant from the Rema Hort Mann Fund .

candidates.text: ​Can You Hear This? Sound-driven creative studio Father investigates transformation from the space between the natural and the analog for the short film Can You Hear This? , asking what a sound becomes once it stops being raw. We set up a mobile studio within Dungeness itself where we spent several days creating music together, inspired by the unique environment which surrounded us. We went to listen, document, and find a state of presence. Capturing the landscapes and soundscapes of Dungeness on England’s Kent coast, the team gathered field recordings by using hydrophones and contact mics on stone, bark, and other materials that don't make sounds, taking the recordings apart and building them into something else entirely. Studying the intersection between raw sounds and process, Can You Hear This? celebrates the act of listening together and the creative possibilities that emerge from it, inspired by the rugged nature of this unique coastal environment.
